items.title: Inferno Cities: Fire incidents and safety compliance
items.standfirst: An analysis of fire accidents in Bangladesh shows how these incidents are not isolated but rather a terrifying reality deeply woven into everyday life.

items.title: The bridge that broke the river
items.standfirst: In 1998, Bangladesh witnessed a milestone: the inauguration of the Jamuna Bridge. The 4.8-kilometre structure across the mighty Jamuna fundamentally transformed connectivity between the northern districts and the capital. But projects of this scale often come with casualties.

items.title: Why Dhaka's waterways matter more than flyovers
items.standfirst: For decades, successive governments have pursued grand solutions — metro rail, flyovers, elevated expressways. Yet experts argue that the answer may already lie beneath our feet: the waterways that once defined this riverine city.

items.title: Faced with fuel shortage, Bangladesh's motorists turn to cooking gas
items.standfirst: The economics of the cheaper alternative are compelling. But the risks, experts say, are not.

items.title: The women the Family Card system could not reach
items.standfirst: The newly-elected government's flagship welfare programme designed for the poorest is helping some people but excluding others, and nobody is fully sure why.
